text: This central district covers Syntagma, Omonoia, Monastiraki, Plaka, Kolonaki, Lycabettus, Exarchia, Koukaki, Ilisia and Makrygianni. It is genuinely two different areas after dark. Omonoia Square has a well-documented, ongoing open drug-dealing problem, with police arrests reported through 2025 and into 2026, including a June 2026 bust in which minors were used as runners. Exarchia has a long-running pattern of anarchist-police clashes and, separately, a June 2026 drug-related shooting that left one person dead. Pickpocketing targeting tourists is a recurring, widely reported issue around the metro system, Syntagma Square and Monastiraki. By contrast, Kolonaki, Plaka, Makrygianni and Koukaki are calm, affluent or tourist-oriented areas with no comparable pattern of documented incidents. Because the district mixes a serious, recurring night-time problem in specific pockets with genuinely quiet, upscale streets a few minutes away, day is rated yellow (pickpocketing risk) and night is rated red overall for the district.

This district covers Pangrati, Zappeion, Mets, Kynosargous, Gouva and Neos Kosmos. Several knifepoint robberies were reported in Pangrati during 2025-2026, including at a betting shop, a gas station and against a taxi driver, and a group knife attack on a 15-year-old was reported in Neos Kosmos. Mets, Zappeion, Kynosargous and Gouva have no documented pattern of incidents in the sources checked. Given the recurring but isolated armed-robbery reports concentrated at night in parts of the district, day is rated green and night is rated yellow.

This district covers Thiseio, Petralona, Rouf, Votanikos and Elaionas. Thiseio and Petralona are described in the city's own official tourism guide as gentrified, pleasant residential and nightlife areas with no documented safety concerns. Votanikos and Elaionas are an industrial fringe area; a 2020 report documented urban decay there, and a refugee reception facility that had operated in the area was evacuated and closed in late 2022, a historical rather than ongoing issue. Rouf shows no documented pattern of incidents in daytime visits or press coverage. Overall the district is rated green by day and yellow at night, reflecting the industrial, sparsely populated character of its western edge after dark rather than any specific documented crime pattern.

This district covers Kolonos, Akadimia Platonos, Kolokynthou, Profitis Daniil and Sepolia, and has one of the most heavily and consistently documented problem patterns in Athens. Sepolia was the scene of a 2021 daylight shooting/execution at a cafe witnessed by a 15-year-old, prompting 2021 citizen patrols against open drug dealing in the area, and in October 2024 police arrested minors dealing drugs outside a primary school there. Kolonos has been repeatedly described in the press as a "new ghetto" (To Vima, 2024; Ta Nea, January 2026) in connection with organised drug dealing near Attika metro station, a gang stabbing, and a 2024 child-exploitation case. Akadimia Platonos was the subject of a 2020 "cry of anguish" report on neglect, balanced by 2024-2025 reporting on an archaeological-park regeneration project underway there. Profitis Daniil has no documented pattern in the sources checked. Given the multi-year, recurring and serious nature of the Sepolia and Kolonos incidents, day is rated yellow and night is rated red.

This district covers Agios Eleftherios, Patisia, Rizoupoli and Prompona. Patisia has a multi-year, well-documented pattern of serious problems: a 2016 Vice report on Kato Patisia, a 2018 LiFO "fear map" naming Patisia as an area residents avoid after dark, a March 2022 knife attack on two women in Ano Patisia, a November 2023 bust of a major drug-trafficking operation involving roughly 24 kilograms of cannabis and cocaine, and a June 2026 knifepoint robbery on Acharnon Street. Rizoupoli and Prompona are quiet residential areas with no documented incidents in the sources checked. Given the sustained, multi-year documentation specific to Patisia, day is rated yellow and night is rated red for the district overall.

This district covers Plateia Amerikis, the Attiki/Victoria Square area, Agios Panteleimonas and Kypseli, and has extensive, multi-year documentation of open drug dealing centred on Attiki and Victoria Squares and Agios Panteleimonas: a 2020 investigative report, a July 2024 crystal-meth arrest, and January 2025 trafficking arrests spanning Kypseli, Agios Panteleimonas and Plateia Amerikis. Agios Panteleimonas also has a documented history of anti-migrant vigilante violence between 2009 and 2012, recorded by Human Rights Watch in over two dozen separate attacks; EU- and municipally-funded redevelopment of the area has been underway since. Central Kypseli, particularly around Fokionos Negri, is explicitly described in the city's own tourism guide as a calm, gentrifying area distinct from the Attiki/Victoria Square pocket. Given the extensive, recurring documentation of drug dealing in specific parts of the district, day is rated yellow and night is rated red.
sources: Human Rights Watch "Hate on the Streets" (2012)

text: This district covers Nea Filothei, Ampelokipoi, Goudi, Kountouriotika, Erythros Stavros, Gyzi and Polygono. Most of the district — Goudi park, Gyzi, Nea Filothei, Polygono and Kountouriotika — is leafy and residential with no documented safety concerns. Ampelokipoi, however, has a real, recurring record of gun violence: a 2021 shooting near the Athens Police headquarters (GADA), an August 2023 shooting outside a lyceum that lightly injured a bystander, and the April 2026 shooting spree by an 89-year-old gunman, whose registered address (confirmed via Athens courthouse records) placed the incident within Ampelokipoi and which wounded four people. A separate incident involving an assault on a nurse at the Red Cross Hospital is a hospital-security matter rather than a street-crime pattern. Given Ampelokipoi's recurring documented gun violence set against an otherwise quiet district, both day and night are rated yellow.
